policy_probe.provenance: Cumulative agent-authored development probes. The latest six wording variants were discovered and fixed in-sample; the total is not blind, independent or representative. Text-only: no attached pixels or attachment metadata processed.

image_routing_dataset.provenance: Agent-authored Vietnamese/English policy development probes. The 2026-10-29 extension from 30 to 36 followed direct policy inspection that found patient-in-clinic, patient-seen, semicolon-linked image, case-from-clinic, person-treated, and person-under-care misses. Query wording informed policy changes on this same dataset; fully in-sample and not independent, blind, clinically adjudicated, or representative. The 2026-10-29 extension from 36 to 41 follows a second policy-boundary review for cross-sentence image references, implicit clinical image ownership, hospital/service patient context, and caregiver wording. These five additions are agent-authored, fully in-sample development probes, not independent or clinically adjudicated. A further 2026-10-29 wording audit extended the development set from 41 to 46 after finding five misses involving Vietnamese patient-image ownership, child film wording, past treatment/consultation wording, and image acquisition followed by a separate sentence. This extension is in-sample and agent-authored, not independent or clinically adjudicated. The v7 extension from 46 to 51 adds five agent-authored personal-image wording probes, remains fully in-sample, and has no independent or specialist adjudication.

reporting_standards_reviewed.name: CLAIM 2024 Update

Consider for a separate BoneScope image-classifier study; select alongside TRIPOD+AI and/or STARD-AI by prespecified aim/design. The 2024 scope excludes radiomics/pathomics. Not a risk-of-bias, validation, retrieval-only RAG or Stage 11 acceptance tool.

reporting_standards_reviewed.name: DECIDE-AI
reporting_standards_reviewed.application: Reporting guideline for early-stage, small-scale live clinical evaluation of AI decision-support: 27 items (17 AI-specific and 10 generic). Reserved for a future live clinical-workflow study; offline retrieval metrics do not satisfy this scope.

reporting_standards_reviewed.name: FDA Clinical Decision Support Software guidance and FAQ
reporting_standards_reviewed.application: Scope note: image analysis does not meet the non-device CDS image-analysis criterion; this alone does not establish device status. Any future use needs a qualified, function- and jurisdiction-specific review.

reporting_standards_reviewed.name: NIST AI Risk Management Framework
reporting_standards_reviewed.application: Voluntary risk-management reference, currently under revision; it is not regulatory approval or clinical validation.

reporting_standards_reviewed.name: WHO Ethics and governance of AI for health
reporting_standards_reviewed.application: Health-AI ethics, human-rights, governance and accountability guidance; it does not certify this project.

reporting_standards_reviewed.name: Vietnam medical-device framework: 08/VBHN-BYT and Circular 24/2026/TT-BYT
reporting_standards_reviewed.application: Conditional jurisdictional lead only. Consolidated Decree 98 text includes software with specified intended medical purposes; Circular 24/2026 is effective 2026-07-01. No classification or pathway determination for BoneScope is made.

reporting_standards_reviewed.name: Vietnam personal and health data governance: Law 91/2025/QH15, Decree 356/2025/NĐ-CP, Decree 102/2025/NĐ-CP
reporting_standards_reviewed.application: Conditional privacy/data-governance review lead before any use of real or identifiable patient information; no legal conclusion or claim of patient-data processing in the current prototype.

reporting_standards_reviewed.name: MI-CLEAR-LLM 2025 update
reporting_standards_reviewed.application: Eight reporting categories for healthcare LLM accuracy studies, including model/access/input/adaptation, prompt optimization/execution, stochasticity and test-set independence. Use for future generator/LLM accuracy work; not retrieval relevance, evidence entailment, abstention validation or approval.

reporting_standards_reviewed.name: FLAIR (Framework for LLM Assessment in Radiology), Radiology 2026
reporting_standards_reviewed.application: Published 2026 radiology-specific LLM reporting checklist (32 items in six categories); complementary aid for future in-scope generator/radiology studies, not a retrieval-only metric or validation. The authors note the search strategy may have missed prior work and that periodic updates may be needed; recheck current version/scope.

reporting_standards_reviewed.name: TRIPOD+AI
reporting_standards_reviewed.application: 2024 reporting guideline for studies developing, evaluating/validating, or updating clinical prediction models using regression or machine learning; 27 main items and 52 subitems. Select alongside STARD-AI only when prespecified study aims/design warrant both. Not a quality appraisal, clinical-validity certification, retrieval-only RAG checklist, or Stage 11 acceptance evidence.

reporting_standards_reviewed.name: TRIPOD-LLM
reporting_standards_reviewed.application: Published 2025 reporting guideline for LLM studies in biomedical/healthcare: 19 main items and 50 subitems; 14 main items/32 subitems apply across designs/tasks, with the remainder modular by research design and LLM task. Use only for an in-scope future LLM study; not a retrieval-only RAG quality/acceptance checklist.

reporting_standards_reviewed.name: CHART
reporting_standards_reviewed.application: Published 2025 reporting guideline for studies evaluating generative chatbots that summarize clinical evidence or provide health advice: 12 items and 39 subitems. Applicable only to future studies in that chatbot-health-advice scope; not to current retrieval-only RAG.

reporting_standards_reviewed.name: SPIRIT 2025
reporting_standards_reviewed.application: Current core protocol reporting guideline (34 items; supersedes SPIRIT 2013). Consider only for a future clinical trial protocol; not a conduct manual or Stage 11 acceptance evidence.

reporting_standards_reviewed.name: CONSORT 2025
reporting_standards_reviewed.application: Current core randomized-trial results reporting guideline (30 items; supersedes CONSORT 2010). Consider only for a future clinical trial report; not a conduct manual or Stage 11 acceptance evidence.

reporting_standards_reviewed.name: SPIRIT-AI
reporting_standards_reviewed.application: 2020 AI-specific protocol extension (15 items: 12 extensions and 3 elaborations) for eligible clinical-trial protocols. The official SPIRIT–CONSORT directory presently lists SPIRIT-AI under SPIRIT 2013 and separately identifies extensions based on SPIRIT 2025. A future trial methodologist must reconcile with current core and journal requirements.

reporting_standards_reviewed.name: CONSORT-AI
reporting_standards_reviewed.application: 2020 AI-specific trial-reporting extension/elaboration (14 items) for eligible AI intervention trials; the BMJ statement describes these as additions to CONSORT 2010. Reconcile with CONSORT 2025 core and journal instructions; do not infer directory listing or automatic harmonization. No trial is in current Stage 11 scope.

reporting_standards_reviewed.name: STARD-AI
reporting_standards_reviewed.application: Published 2025 reporting guideline for diagnostic-accuracy studies of AI index tests against a reference standard (40 checklist items); use for a future prespecified classifier or diagnostic-output study in scope. The 2026 author correction changes steering-committee listing, not the checklist. Not for current retrieval-only RAG, risk-of-bias appraisal, validation certification or gate closure.

reporting_standards_reviewed.name: SPIRIT-C 2026
reporting_standards_reviewed.application: 2026 extension adding 17 protocol-reporting items for randomized trials involving children/adolescents aged 0–19; use alongside SPIRIT 2025 only for an in-scope paediatric RCT. Not current retrieval-only evaluation or conduct/acceptance evidence.

reporting_standards_reviewed.name: CONSORT-C 2026
reporting_standards_reviewed.application: 2026 extension adding 13 results-reporting items for randomized trials involving children/adolescents aged 0–19; use alongside CONSORT 2025 only for an in-scope paediatric RCT. Not current retrieval-only evaluation or conduct/acceptance evidence.

reporting_standards_reviewed.name: GAMER
reporting_standards_reviewed.application: 2025 nine-item reporting guideline for use of generative AI in any phase of medical research or manuscript preparation. It reports tool use/role; it does not assess performance or clinical validity of the AI system being studied and does not replace design-specific reporting guidance or retrieval-only RAG evaluation.

reporting_standards_reviewed.name: CLAIM 2026 Explanation, Elaboration and Examples
reporting_standards_reviewed.application: Companion explanation/elaboration and illustrative examples for the 44-item CLAIM 2024 Update. Helps reviewers interpret the existing items; it is not a new checklist or revision, appraisal, validation, or Stage 11 acceptance gate.

targeted_cohort_search_refresh.result: No new publicly reusable patient-level independent cohort with adequate reference standard surfaced. Frontiers 2026 uses BTXRD with image-level 750 test split; its 11-case external series is tumour-positive only and explicitly exploratory without study-team reannotation/adjudication. DeepTIRP has 423 external patients for a tumor-versus-infection endpoint but Zenodo data are restricted, request/MTA/IRB required, article DOI 13858807 differs from matching-title Zenodo record 13858808, and visible license absent. Keep as permission request candidate only; no dataset accessed. Official issue-index abstract for Huang/Yao/Li 2024 now confirms 2,127 cases from six facilities (2013-2022), multimodality inputs and binary X-ray model AUC 0.8499. Yao Shunhan and Huang Yuanxiang also author the BTXRD descriptor, with overlapping Guangxi collection windows; this elevates lineage clarification priority without proving case/image overlap. No portal, data-specific reuse license or patient-level manifest verified; lead only.

new_bone_tumor_vlm_rag_study.citation: Shi Y, Tong ZC. Diagnostic Performance of a Locally Deployed Vision Language Model for Bone Tumor Diagnosis Using Smartphone-Captured Images: Exploratory Retrospective Study. JMIR AI. 2026;5:e99757.
new_bone_tumor_vlm_rag_study.design: Single-center exploratory 2x2 evaluation: one Qwen3-VL 32B Thinking Q4 checkpoint, persona x RAG; 42 biopsy-confirmed tumor/tumor-like cases; smartphone screen-captured X-ray/CT/MRI, 3-5 slices per case selected by one specialist.
new_bone_tumor_vlm_rag_study.reported_result: Radiologist-persona top-1 was 12/42 (29%, 95% CI 16%-45%) without RAG vs 6/42 (14%, 95% CI 5%-29%) with RAG (McNemar P=.03); orthopedic-oncologist persona had no significant top-1/top-3 change as reported.
reported_limitations: Exploratory, single center, small cohort and single model.
No clean-image control or blinded human comparator.
One specialist selected slices without blinded independent adjudication.
Subgroup comparisons were not corrected for multiplicity; p values nominal.
Cohort mixes modalities and contains tumor/tumor-like cases only; not an eligible external test for BoneScope X-ray classifier.
new_bone_tumor_vlm_rag_study.data_rights: Article states CC BY 4.0. It lists five appendices of original input images, but also says the complete generated/analyzed dataset is not public because of privacy and institutional health-data protection and may be shared on reasonable request subject to institutional/ethics approval. File-level image rights, data-use authority, de-identification, provenance and checkpoint overlap are not verified for BoneScope.
new_bone_tumor_vlm_rag_study.disposition: Risk-identification literature only; do not transfer performance or thresholds to BoneScope; no download, registration or ingestion. Any future request/reuse requires custodian review, rights/privacy authority, manifest, endpoint mapping and overlap clearance.
new_bone_tumor_vlm_rag_study.verification_basis: Official JMIR article landing page, abstract, methods, limitations, data availability, supplementary-file list and license. Reviewed 2026-10-29.

kjr_2026_reader_assistance_followup.citation: Kim DK et al. Enhancing Radiologists’ Diagnostic Performance for Primary Bone Tumors Using Structured Report-Driven Assistance From Multiple Large Language Models. Korean Journal of Radiology. 2026. doi:10.3348/kjr.2026.0593.
kjr_2026_reader_assistance_followup.open_access_license: CC BY-NC 4.0 for article text; not evidence of image or patient-dataset reuse rights.
kjr_2026_reader_assistance_followup.design: Retrospective single-center Seoul St. Mary’s Hospital; 525 pathologically confirmed primary bone tumor cases screened (Jan 2019-Jan 2026), 293 excluded; 15 prompt-development cases and 217 reader-evaluation cases; three MSK radiologists with 17, 6, and 1 years experience.
kjr_2026_reader_assistance_followup.workflow: Readers first interpreted images and produced structured text reports plus ranked Top-3. After six-week washout and newly randomized order they re-read cases; four-LLM pipeline received final structured report and clinical complaint, not image pixels in the described pipeline. Radiologists reviewed suggestions and made final diagnosis while viewing images.
kjr_2026_reader_assistance_followup.human_factors: Less-experienced reader more often accepted incorrect suggestions; most-experienced reader rejected incorrect suggestions more often but also rejected correct suggestions more often. Authors describe top-1 harm including clinically concerning malignant/intermediate-to-benign downgrades; harm and second-look effects merit prespecified review.
limitations: Single center and no external validation.
Only three readers; reader-specific effect exploratory.
Retrospective biopsy/pathology-confirmed enriched challenging cohort; metastases and many typical benign lesions excluded.
Potential second-look effect after repeated reading.
Structured reports were human-generated; text translation can omit image detail and routine free-text generalization is unknown.
Data available from corresponding author on reasonable request; no dataset/images accessed or requested here.
kjr_2026_reader_assistance_followup.stage_disposition: Future generated-differential human-factors/automation-bias hazard literature only. Not an image-VLM study, not a retrieval-only RAG evaluation, not a BoneScope estimate, and not an eligible external cohort. No BoneScope acceptance threshold inferred.
kjr_2026_reader_assistance_followup.verified_from: Official publisher full text, abstract, methods, results, discussion, limitations, and data-availability statement; reviewed 2026-10-29.
